article.title: NFL EDGE Monday Morning Brief
article.dek: Washington closes Sunday with a 27-10 win, Baltimore's quarterback room is down to one healthy arm before Thursday night, and Monday night in Seattle is the last game left on the Week 8 board.

items.headline: Lead: Washington closes Sunday 27-10 — one game left on the Week 8 board
paragraphs: Washington beat Philadelphia 27-10 on Sunday night, scoring 27 unanswered points after falling behind 10-0 in the first quarter. Jayden Daniels threw for 217 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions, while Tanner McKee threw for 212 yards with one interception in his third start in place of Jalen Hurts. Philadelphia has now lost six straight, its first six-game losing streak since 2012.

That leaves exactly one game on the Week 8 board: Chicago at Seattle, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET. The morning board's cards are all on that game — Seattle moneyline for Hit Rate, Chicago +3 for both Balanced and Value. See below for what each card means.

One thing is still to come, and it is the only thing worth waiting for: Monday night's inactive lists, about 90 minutes before kickoff, for the questionable names below. Check them before you lock anything in.
items.takeaway: Washington 27-10 closes Sunday; Chicago at Seattle on Monday night is the only Week 8 game left, and its inactive lists are the last update before kickoff.

items.headline: Injury roundup: Baltimore down to one healthy quarterback; Seattle's line reshuffles for Monday
paragraphs: Baltimore's quarterback situation got worse overnight. Lamar Jackson will have surgery on his right thumb and go on injured reserve after getting hurt on the first offensive play at Buffalo, missing at least four games — and head coach Jesse Minter said the injury could potentially end his season. Backup Tyler Huntley hurt his toe in the same game, is being evaluated for suspected turf toe, and has an MRI on Monday; reports say he could miss Thursday night's home game against Jacksonville. That leaves undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who finished the Buffalo game at 10-of-21 for 91 yards with one interception, as the only healthy quarterback on the roster as Monday begins. No Thursday starter has been announced — that is the injury story to watch this week, not something to guess at today.

For Monday night, Seattle's offensive line gets reshuffled. Starting left tackle Charles Cross is out with an ankle injury, so Josh Jones steps in at left tackle, newly acquired Quenton Nelson debuts at left guard, and Grey Zabel shifts to right guard. Chicago is without running back Kyle Monangai (toe) for a fourth straight game, Seattle is without receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee) and running back Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Uchenna Nwosu is doubtful (ankle), and Chicago's D'Marco Jackson (ankle) and Malik Muhammad (toe) are questionable.

One return to note: Seattle running back Zach Charbonnet is set to play for the first time since tearing his ACL last postseason, after surgery in February and activation from the physically unable to perform list on Oct. 22. Questionable does not mean out — the inactive lists about 90 minutes before kickoff are the next real update.
items.takeaway: Jackson is headed for thumb surgery and injured reserve, Huntley may miss Thursday with a toe injury, and Monday's questionables still wait on the inactive lists.

items.headline: Weather: cool and cloudy for Monday night in Seattle
paragraphs: Monday night in Seattle looks cool and cloudy. The National Weather Service hourly forecast has about 49 degrees around the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, cloudy skies, a light north-northwest wind of about 2 mph, and an 8 percent chance of precipitation, with temperatures holding around 48 to 49 degrees through the evening.
That is the forecast as it stands Monday morning, reported as fact. It is not a reason to bet a total one way or the other.
items.takeaway: Seattle Monday night: about 49 degrees at kickoff, cloudy, light wind, 8 percent rain chance.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Morning cards: Seattle moneyline on top, Chicago +3 fills both other cards
paragraphs: Hit Rate is the Seattle moneyline at -175 at DraftKings, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET against Chicago. It is the pick the app rates most likely to win, with a model probability of 0.561. Remember the app's own tutorial: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. A favorite's moneyline can look safe and still pay very little — you are betting on the outright winner only.
Balanced is Chicago +3 at -102 at DraftKings, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET at Seattle. It is a strong pick without paying too much — the middle ground, and a good starting point for a new bettor.

Value is Chicago +3 at -102 at DraftKings as well — the same pick as Balanced. Value is always the model's +EV play, and this morning that play and the Balanced play land on the same line. Two cards pointing at the same pick is not two separate bets; it is one pick the app likes two ways.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate: Seattle moneyline -175. Balanced and Value: both Chicago +3 -102 at DraftKings — one pick, liked two ways.

items.headline: A card that changes still means checking your own price
paragraphs: The cards above are priced at DraftKings. If your book is not DraftKings, the card price is not your price.

Tap Check in the app, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. That is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

Odds are price mechanics: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and staking setting — that part is deliberately conservative, and it lives in the app, not here.
items.takeaway: Your book's price is the one that matters — run it through Check and let that verdict decide.

items.headline: Learn the Game: the vig
paragraphs: The vig — short for vigorish, also called the juice — is the book's cut, built into the price itself. It is why both sides of a spread usually sit at -110 instead of even money.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say you bet a spread at -110. That price means you risk $1.10 to win $1.00. Win, and you get your $1.10 back plus $1.00. Lose, and the $1.10 is gone. The extra 10 cents on each side is the book's margin for taking the bet.

That is why a price move matters even when the line does not move: -102 and -115 on the same +3 are not the same bet. When you run a price through Check, the app prices the vig in — a good line at a bad price can still come back no-bet.
items.takeaway: The vig is the book's cut built into the price — at -110 you risk $1.10 to win $1.00, so the price itself is part of the bet.

items.headline: Evening board vs morning board: Seattle moneyline gets pricier, Chicago +3 changes books, Value returns
paragraphs: Hit Rate stays the Seattle moneyline, but it gets pricier: from -166 at DraftKings on the evening board to -175 at DraftKings this morning, with the play-through price moving from -171 to -180. Same pick, more expensive than it was Sunday evening.
Balanced stays Chicago +3 at -102, but the book changes: from FanDuel on the evening board to DraftKings this morning, with the play-through price still -105. Same pick, same price, different book.
Value comes back. The evening board had no Value play; this morning Chicago +3 at -102 at DraftKings satisfies the Value lane, so the lane is filled again — with the same pick as Balanced.

Everything else on the Week 8 board is final, so there is no other movement to report. The morning refresh caught all of it. If your book shows something different from the prices above, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and let the app re-evaluate it for you.
items.takeaway: Seattle moneyline -166 to -175, Chicago +3 stays -102 but moves from FanDuel to DraftKings, and Value returns with Chicago +3.

items.headline: Monday game? Monday check.
paragraphs: There is one piece of information worth waiting for: Monday night's inactive lists, about 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, for the questionable names above. That is a real pending event with a set time.

Everything else is ready now. If your book has a good number on Chicago +3 or the Seattle moneyline and Check says bet, bet now — waiting for the Monday night rush lets the number drift the wrong way too.
items.takeaway: Wait only for Monday night's inactive lists; otherwise bet when Check says bet.

Sunday Night Football final, Nov. 1: Washington beat Philadelphia 27-10 at Northwest Stadium. Philadelphia led 10-0 in the first quarter, then Washington scored 27 unanswered points. Jayden Daniels finished 16-of-29 for 217 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions; Tanner McKee finished 23-of-34 for 212 yards with one interception in his third start in place of Jalen Hurts; Saquon Barkley scored Philadelphia's only touchdown. Philadelphia fell to 2-6 with its sixth straight loss, its first six-game losing streak since 2012; Washington improved to 2-4-1.

Baltimore quarterback news, Monday morning, Nov. 2: Lamar Jackson will have surgery on his right thumb and go on injured reserve after getting hurt on Baltimore's first offensive play of the 36-10 loss at Buffalo, missing at least four games; head coach Jesse Minter said the injury could potentially end Jackson's season. Backup Tyler Huntley suffered a toe injury in the same game, is being evaluated for suspected turf toe, and has an MRI on Monday; reports say he could miss Thursday night's home game against Jacksonville. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finished the Buffalo game (10-of-21, 91 yards, one interception) and is the only healthy quarterback on the roster as Monday begins. Baltimore hosts Jacksonville on Thursday night.

Monday Night Football injury picture, CHI at SEA, Nov. 2, 8:15 p.m. ET: Seattle starting LT Charles Cross ruled out (ankle, suffered Oct. 25 vs Kansas City, no practice all week); Josh Jones starts at left tackle, newly acquired Quenton Nelson debuts at left guard, Grey Zabel shifts to right guard. Chicago RB Kyle Monangai (toe) ruled out, his fourth straight missed game; LB D'Marco Jackson (ankle) and CB Malik Muhammad (toe) questionable; TE Colston Loveland (neck) cleared, LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring) returning. Seattle WR Rashid Shaheed (knee) out, LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) doubtful, QB Drew Lock (elbow), G Anthony Bradford (knee), DT Brandon Pili (back), LB Patrick O'Connell (toe) questionable.

Seattle running back Zach Charbonnet is set to play Monday night against Chicago, his first game since tearing his ACL in last postseason's divisional-round win over San Francisco on Jan. 17; he had surgery in February and was activated from the physically unable to perform list on Oct. 22. Rookie running back Jadarian Price was declared ready to play but still had to be activated off injured reserve.

National Weather Service hourly forecast for Seattle, checked Monday morning, Nov. 2: at the Monday night kickoff window (8:15 p.m. ET, 5:15 p.m. Seattle time), 49 degrees, cloudy, about a 2 mph north-northwest wind, and an 8 percent chance of precipitation, with temperatures holding around 48-49 degrees through the evening.
